text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock rose 2.8% today after falling sharply over the past two weeks, rebounding from what appears to be a sharp selloff on October 27th when the stock dropped $34 in a single day. The bounce today follows crude oil's decline on November 2nd amid peace talk hopes between the U.S. and Iran—which typically signals lower geopolitical risk and more stable energy markets. Refining utilization remains solid at 92.8%, and while crude prices have come under pressure (U.S. oil at $103/barrel versus higher levels earlier in the month), the company announced a leadership change and update on October 29th that may have also contributed to today's modest recovery in investor sentiment.

The stock's two-week decline of 7% likely reflects broader caution among investors heading into Big Oil earnings season, where forward guidance matters as much as reported profits. The company operates in an environment of moderating oil prices and mixed signals—geopolitical tensions that could support crude are being offset by hopes for diplomatic resolution, leaving refiners in a holding pattern on both input costs and demand outlook.
